prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM System. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (own authority). Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. System: Regional Flow Platform alias Cedarbell (coordination only). Parts: Demand Prediction Service alias Marlinstone, Capacity Assessment Module (CAM), Slot Allocation Engine (feasibility only), Airport CDM Portal alias Foxglove, Digital Briefing Room, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console (both only under accountable roles), Contingency Operations Console, Weather Ingest Gateway alias Orchard, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub, Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log, North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display. Actors: Regional Flow Manager alias Copperfin (owns intent; reviews Airport Capacity Plan, Ground Delay Program, Tactical Regulation Proposal; authorizes measures; confirms airline recovery priorities before revised constraints published); Airline Operations Coordinator alias Saffron (keeps Flight Intent Message status, Target Off Block Time, passenger readiness indicator, aircraft constraint notes current); Slot Coordinator; Meteorology Briefing Officer (Storm Cell Snapshot); Airport Duty Manager (monitors Common Situation Display vs terminal/passenger capacity); Tower Supervisor (Runway Inspection Note; reviews metering in Tower Sequence Manager); Ramp Control Lead (checks recovery vs surface congestion on Ramp Movement Board); Ground Handling Dispatcher (Crew Bus Delay Slip); Handling Resource Planner; Airspace Sector Planner, Aircraft Operator Representative, Network Operations Liaison, Deicing Coordinator, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Data Governance Steward, System Support Engineer. Flows: airlines→Flight Intent Message→Airline Interface Adapter (validates via Business Rules Registry; rejects with reasons)→Flight Data Exchange→Marlinstone; Orchard→CAM (Airport Capacity Plan, Airport Acceptance Rate, Storm Cell Snapshot). Disputes→Collaborative Decision Log (airline, rationale, owner, resolution). Adverse Weather/Capacity Reduction: conservative intents, firm vs speculative. Recovery Phase: frequent updates, prior values retained. Airline transactions time-stamped (Time Synchronization Service)→Audit Event Ledger. Performance Analytics Warehouse compares intents, constraints, off-block, arrivals. Foxglove

New part:
S158: The Ground Handling Dispatcher is responsible for updating servicing completion, baggage readiness, staffing limitation, and equipment availability milestones as soon as the handling status changes.
S159: The Ramp Control Lead is responsible for maintaining stand release readiness, apron movement conflicts, tug availability, and local pushback sequencing inputs in the portal.
S160: The Tower Supervisor is responsible for reviewing runway configuration assumptions, departure sequence feasibility, and tactical tower constraints before those values are used for metering decisions.
S161: The Slot Coordinator is responsible for checking Calculated Takeoff Time feasibility and recording accepted slot adjustments, rejected slot adjustments, and unresolved slot conflicts in the Collaborative Decision Log.
S162: The Airport Duty Manager is responsible for maintaining the Airport Capacity Plan, declaring local operating impacts, and confirming transitions between Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase.
S163: The Meteorology Briefing Officer uses the portal workspace to attach weather interpretation, forecast confidence, and expected timing of operational impacts without replacing the authoritative weather source.
S164: Cedarbell shall expose the current regional demand and constraint context to the shared workspace at each publication cycle without requiring manual re-entry.
S165: The Common Situation Display distinguishes values supplied by connected services, values confirmed by users, and values that have exceeded the configured freshness threshold.
S166: When a milestone becomes stale, the Airport CDM Portal shall highlight the affected flight and notify the role accountable for the next update through the Alert Distribution Hub.
S167: Each airport participant shall update a material change within two minutes of becoming aware of it during Normal Operations and within one minute during Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State.
S168: If the exact value is not yet known, the accountable participant shall enter a provisional value with an uncertainty flag rather than leaving the milestone unchanged.
S169: The Collaborative Decision Log records who changed a value, when the change was made, whether the change was provisional or confirmed, and what operational decision relied on it.
S170: The Data Governance Steward defines the mandatory fields, permissible status values, retention rules, and data quality thresholds used by the Airport CDM Portal.
S171: The System Support Engineer monitors portal availability, interface latency, user session faults, and synchronization status against the Time Synchronization Service.
S172: During Contingency Fallback State, the Airport CDM Portal shall preserve the last synchronized milestone set and clearly mark any updates entered under degraded operating procedures.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
